description_plain:
Our Firm

Agentis Capital Advisors is a leading global financial advisor with a reputation for delivering unparalleled value and advice to its clients. The firm has been the recipient of numerous recent industry rewards, including Financial Advisor of the Year in North America by P3 Awards (2024), Proximo (2022), and IJGlobal (2021). 

The Opportunity

Our Associate program is designed to cultivate the quantitative and qualitative skills necessary to excel in an investment banking career. You will receive both formal and on-the-job training throughout your tenure. You will gain increasing levels of responsibility as you progress in your career, from overseeing the execution of financial model-related tasks, to managing multiple deal workstreams, to leading client relationships. You will be given unparalleled exposure and opportunities, including the chance to lead numerous transactions. As a result, our team members often achieve accelerated career growth and earn industry recognition. You will be recognized and rewarded for your individual performance within a close-knit team and meritocratic culture. 



Your Contribution

As an integral member of the global public-private partnership (P3) advisory team, you will be challenged to accept increasing levels of responsibility as you develop your skills and reputation. Your work will directly impact our clients and the firm.

Your role will include:

 - Participating in the execution of PPP transactions

 - Developing complex financial models, including the use of macros and VBA programming

 - Assisting in the management of due diligence processes, including managing third-party advisors

 - Preparing client presentations and actively participating in discussions

 - Researching potential business development opportunities

 - Maintaining marketing materials for the firm, including creating pitches to be presented to potential clients

As a member of a high-performing team working in a fast-paced environment, there will be times where you will be required to work beyond a normal workday or workweek to fulfill the responsibilities of the role.



Our Differentiators

Breadth of experience and level of responsibility

 - Exceptional level of responsibility on complex transactions, allowing for rapid career progression

 - Opportunities to work on large global transactions

Training

 - Continuous internal training program

 - Internal leadership development program

Culture and approach

 - Entrepreneurial culture with a flat organization structure

 - Direct exposure to Partners and senior management across Agentis' offices

 - Defined path to achieving Partner, with all individuals entering the organization receiving the opportunity to become a full Partner in the business

Compensation and employee ownership

 - Uncapped performance-based bonus

 - Employee ownership program that commences for all individuals from the end of their first full fiscal-year of employment

Other benefits

 - Paid sabbatical every two years of employment

 - Comprehensive benefits including extended health care
   
   

Your Skills and Experience

 - A minimum of 2-3 years of experience in PPP transactions, including financial modeling

 - Ability to concisely communicate complex concepts and ideas verbally and in writing

 - Ability to take initiative and work independently with minimal supervision

 - Desire to assume increasing levels of responsibility and seek solutions to complex problems

 - Committed to producing accurate and thorough work product under tight deadlines

 - Ability to learn quickly and adapt in a fast-paced work environment

 - Resilient mindset in the face of adversity

 - Ability to work effectively in a team environment
   
   

Position Type

 - Permanent Full-Time

 - Desired start date: Immediately

 - Location: Vancouver or Toronto

description_plain:
Vice President



Duties: Develop and manage client relationships globally across the financial institutions sector, primarily within insurance services and distribution, and closely related insurance brokerage, employee benefits, and insurance technology services businesses. Serve as trusted day-to-day point of contact for clients and partner with senior bankers to advance client dialogues and deliver strategic advice. Lead end-to-end execution of multiple insurance services and distribution transactions, including reviewing valuation and financial analysis, coordinating due diligence, drafting and reviewing marketing and board materials, and managing internal deal teams and external parties. Manage and develop Associates and Analysts, providing ongoing training, mentoring, and performance feedback. Act as a technical subject-matter expert on insurance services and distribution accounting and regulatory topics, as well as on core corporate finance and capital markets concepts. Own delegation, quality control, and risk management for transaction execution and client deliverables by dividing responsibilities and setting timelines, enforcing review gates and ensuring compliant handling of MNPI, conflicts/KYC, and recordkeeping. Champion a culture of excellence, integrity, and collaboration by modeling leadership standards and reinforcing best practices across execution teams.



Requirements: Requires Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or related field of study, and 4 years of experience as Associate or Analyst involving financial modeling, valuation analysis, transaction execution, due diligence, and preparation of client-facing materials for financial institutions in the investment banking or a related industry. Will accept Master’s degree and 3 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor’s degree and 4 years of experience. Experience specified must include 4 years of experience (3 years if Master’s degree) with each of the following: leading financial modeling, valuation, transaction structuring and process-related workstreams across multiple transactions; one or more financial data platforms (e.g., Bloomberg, Capital IQ and SNL, FactSet, PitchBook, or comparable); performing financial analysis and modeling, including building integrated three-statement financial models, discounted cash flow (DCF) analysis, leveraged buyout (LBO) analysis, accretion/dilution analysis, and comparable company and precedent transaction analyses; mergers and acquisitions (M&A), including buy-side and sell-side advisory, divestitures, joint ventures, recapitalizations, management buyouts (MBOs), and leveraged buyouts (LBOs), as well as familiarity with fairness opinions and valuation advisory services; U.S. GAAP, SEC regulations, and investment banking compliance standards; and using Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Experience specified must also include 3 years of experience with each of the following: reviewing teasers, confidential information memoranda (CIMs), management presentations, and due diligence materials; managing multiple multi-party transaction processes in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment; mentoring and developing junior bankers; reviewing and providing feedback on financial analyses, models, and presentation materials prepared by junior team members; supporting client relationship management and business development efforts in coordination with senior bankers, including pitch preparation and client communications; and communicating analytical findings and transaction considerations to senior clients and internal stakeholders. Experience specified must include 2 years of experience in the insurance services and distribution industry, including experience with insurance services and distribution business models, regulatory frameworks, key performance metrics and execution of live transactions. Telecommuting permitted up to 1 day per week. Requires up to 20% domestic travel.



Employer: Ardea Services LLC

Work Location: 10 Hudson Yards 48th Floor, New York, NY 10001

Hours: M-F, 40 hours/week

Salary: $325,000/year

description_plain:
Our Firm

Agentis Capital Advisors is a leading global financial advisor with a reputation for delivering unparalleled value and strategic advice to its clients. Agentis acts as a sell-side and buy-side advisor with a focus on global transactions involving infrastructure, renewable power, energy, digital, transportation, and public-private partnerships.

With more than $125 billion in evaluated transactions and multiple industry awards, including North American Financial Advisor of the Year, we apply disciplined thinking, practical innovation, and an ownership mindset to every mandate. Our guiding principles and ability to generate value are our differentiators, which have earned the trust, respect, and business from leading infrastructure funds, pension funds, contractors, and governments.


Our Differentiators

 - Direct responsibility on complex, high-profile transactions across verticals and financial products

 - Direct involvement in SPAC and de-SPAC initiatives, with the opportunity to participate in associated economics

 - Competitive compensation with meaningful employee ownership and full benefits

 - Structured training and leadership development, including direct mentorship from Partners

 - Paid sabbatical every two years of employment

 - Entrepreneurial culture with a defined and achievable path to partnership

 - Co-investment rights alongside Partners on select principal opportunities
   

The Opportunity

Due to growth and an expanding remit across public-market acquisition vehicles, Agentis Capital Advisors is seeking a Managing Director, Investment Banking to lead and grow its digital infrastructure practice.

The Managing Director will play a pivotal role as part of the leadership team for Agentis’ North American investment banking practice, splitting time between (i) originating financial advisory mandates across digital infrastructure (and adjacent verticals), and (ii) leading and supporting SPAC and de-SPAC origination and execution across publicly listed acquisition vehicles. As a subject matter expert in digital infrastructure (including data centers, fiber, and towers), the Managing Director will also provide deal execution leadership and mentorship to junior bankers across the team.

The ideal candidate is an accomplished M&A banker with deep digital infrastructure sector expertise, a track record of sourcing and winning mandates, and a reputation for outstanding client service. An established network of existing or prospective clients in North America is expected.



Key Responsibilities

Deal Origination & Revenue Generation:

 - Identify and pursue new M&A advisory opportunities in digital infrastructure (such as data centers, fiber, and towers) and adjacent energy verticals, aligned with Agentis’ platform and growth strategy

 - Lead and support SPAC target origination and de-SPAC execution, screening private and public companies against SPAC-over-alternatives criteria

 - Lead pitch presentations to win mandates with the support of a talented, experienced team

 - Meet individual and firm revenue targets through successful deal closures, including SPAC and de-SPAC mandates

Senior Client Relationship Management:

 - Serve as the primary point of contact for investors, C-suite executives, board members, and government officials.

 - Build long-term partnerships with institutional investors such as pension funds, private wealth offices, and infrastructure private equity firms.

Strategic Advisory:

 - Provide senior counsel on M&A, capital raising, and complex financing structures across digital infrastructure and adjacent verticals

 - Originate and support financial advisory mandates as required, drawing on sector expertise and target-screening capability across private and public-market opportunities

 - Advise clients on the impact of market dynamics, industry trends, and regulatory developments

Leadership & Team Mentorship:

 - Lead, motivate, and mentor deal teams to meet execution deliverables, staffing commitments, and performance objectives

 - Assist in the recruitment and development of top talent to maintain a competitive practice

Deal Execution Oversight:

 - Oversee end-to-end execution of advisory mandates and de-SPAC mandates, ensuring work product, timelines, and commercial terms align with client and firm standards
   

Skills and Experience

 - Minimum ten years of investment banking or financial advisory experience with a digital infrastructure focus (data centers, fiber, and towers), and a proven track record in origination, business development, and client relationship management

 - Demonstrated ability to structure, execute, and close sell-side M&A and related advisory mandates

 - Familiarity with SPAC / de-SPAC processes and public company M&A is strongly preferred

 - Strong deal management and technical delivery capabilities

 - Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills

 - Ability to work under pressure and consistently deliver high-quality work with strict deadlines to meet team and client objectives (often while being geographically dispersed)

 - Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally as required

 - While all qualified investment professionals are encouraged to apply, this role is specifically scoped to a digital infrastructure background.
   

Position Type

 - Permanent Full-Time

 - Location: Toronto or Vancouver

 - Desired start date: Immediately

description_plain:
WHO WE ARE

Bristlecone Companies https://www.bristleconecompanies.com/ is a permanent capital holding company that acquires and builds mission-critical businesses with one defining characteristic: customers who don’t leave. We are company builders at heart, committed to deepening customer relationships, creating environments where talented people thrive, and amplifying the legacies of founders who have entrusted us with their life’s work.

While our mandate is broad, our approach is focused: we develop deep domain expertise and partner with management teams to build enduring market leaders through both organic and inorganic growth. We seek essential businesses with predictable cash flow, exceptional retention, and leading positions in specialized markets. Our investment discipline is grounded in deep fundamental research, and our ownership philosophy is defined by decentralization, continuous improvement, and an indefinite time horizon.

Rooted in an ethos of stewardship, we find meaning in the work itself, in the pride of ownership, and in the quiet rigor of doing things the right way. Our team is lean by design: autonomy is given early, standards are high, and the reward for great work is more responsibility. If you are driven, deeply curious, and energized by the opportunity to build alongside people who share your standards and ambition, you will thrive here.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

We’ve established a quality foundation through our first acquisitions. In this next chapter, we’re hiring an Investment Lead to help build our acquisition engine — a core competency that will compound over time and determine the quality of businesses we own. Joining at a formative stage, you’ll partner directly with the CEO to build the investment function from the ground up, serve as the first layer of judgment in our investment process, and drive opportunities through close with full ownership pre-LOI. More specifically, you will:

 - Develop investment theses and proactively source businesses through research, referrals, and persistent outreach to owners and industry participants.

 - Cultivate long-term, trust-based relationships with business owners and with the brokers and intermediaries who represent them.

 - Evaluate businesses with your own investment judgment and advance the strongest to actionable opportunities.

 - Support transaction structuring, negotiation, and execution in partnership with the CEO.

 - Collaborate with operating company leadership on post-acquisition strategy and add-on acquisitions.

 - Build and continuously improve the systems that make sourcing and diligence repeatable and scalable.

Success will be measured by the quality and consistency of deal flow and, ultimately, closed acquisitions. Over time, you will have the opportunity to become a key partner in building and scaling Bristlecone.




WHO YOU ARE

While we care far more about who you are than where you've been, the role is best suited for someone with 1-5 years of investing experience in private equity, growth equity, or serial acquirors. More importantly:

 - A proven originator — you've sourced 1-3 proprietary acquisitions per year, ideally platform investments in the lower middle market valued on cash flow or EBITDA

 - Strong investment judgment with commercial fluency across business quality, financial performance, and market structure

 - Clear, crisp, and thoughtful communicator who establishes trust and credibility quickly through authenticity, humility, and reliability

 - Relentless and resilient, thriving in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment

 - Insatiably curious, actively reflective, and quick to update your beliefs and approach based on feedback and outcomes

 - A builder at heart — energized by shaping something from the ground up and genuinely motivated by building a sourcing engine and durable businesses that compound with time



This role is based in Chicago with frequent travel to build differentiated relationships with owners in person. Compensation includes a competitive base salary, uncapped bonus potential, and meaningful equity participation structured for long-term compounding.

description_plain:
ABOUT TURN/RIVER

Turn/River Capital is a private equity firm that applies a proprietary growth engineering strategy to investing, partnering with software businesses to accelerate growth and build enduring value. The firm’s team of equal parts investors and operators provides hands-on operational support and the flexible capital to systematically scale marketing, sales and customer success at its portfolio companies. Founded in 2012 and based in San Francisco, Turn/River has $5.6bn in committed capital and invests globally with a focus on North America and Europe.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Senior Fund Accountant to join our finance team. Reporting directly to the VP of Fund Finance, this individual will help oversee the accounting and financial reporting activities of the firm's investment funds and related entities. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, partnering across functions, and contributing within a lean team where strong performance is rewarded with increased responsibility and growth.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Review quarterly and annual financial statements prepared by the fund administrator

 - Liaise with the funds’ service providers (fund administrator, auditor, etc.)

 - Analyze investment transactions to ensure appropriate reflection in the funds’ accounting records

 - Monitor cash activity and planning for the funds, including cash projections, line of credit advance requests, paydowns, and bank compliance

 - Assist with capital call and distribution calculations

 - Respond to investor inquiries and support financial reporting requests

 - Review investor statements and related communications

 - Ensure efficient, well-documented day-to-day processes and detailed accounting review

 - Contribute to ad hoc projects, including process improvements and AI-related initiatives




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3-4+ years of experience of public and/or private accounting experience

 - Exposure to fund accounting within private equity, venture capital, hedge funds, or similar investment vehicles 

 - Strong and demonstrated interest in accounting

 - Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail

 - Ability to manage and prioritize multiple workstreams in a deadline-driven environment

 - Proactive, adaptable, and brings a hands-on, team-first mentality

 - Strong work ethic with a commitment to quality

 - Thinks ahead, anticipates needs, and proactively identifies opportunities for improvement

 - CPA (active or inactive) a plus

 - Bachelors degree




LOCATION

 - San Francisco, hybrid work model.  
   
    


COMPENSATION

 - The annual base salary range for this role is $130,000 - $135,000, plus an annual performance bonus, taking into account numerous variable factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience, training, licensure, certifications, and organizational requirements.

 


BENEFITS AND PERKS

The below benefits are offered to full-time employees based out of our San Francisco office:

 - An opportunity to make an impact across multiple high-growth tech firms

 - Competitive salary and discretionary bonus

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance covered 100% for employee & dependents

 - Flexible vacation policy

 - 401K matching

 - Paid parental leave

 - Commuter benefits

 - Health and Wellness benefits

 - Household Services benefits

 - Home Office benefits

 - Annual Home Office Equipment Reimbursement

 - Donation matching

 - Work from home Monday & Friday

 - Energetic work environment with snacks and weekly team lunches 3x per week, centrally located near multiple public transit lines

 - A company that enjoys having fun: holiday parties, annual company offsite and retreat, annual summer "work from anywhere" month

The firm’s team of equal parts investors and operators provides hands-on operational support and the flexible capital to systematically scale marketing, sales and customer success at its portfolio companies. Founded in 2012 and based in San Francisco, Turn/River has $5.6bn in committed capital and invests globally with a focus on North America and Europe.



About the Role

Turn/River is seeking a VP, Talent Partner to work directly with our portfolio companies to assess, design, and strengthen their executive and go-to-market organizations. This role sits at the intersection of talent strategy, organizational design, and commercial performance — with a primary focus on executive and go-to-market teams.

You will bring deep expertise in executive search best practices, leadership assessment, and org design — and you will apply that expertise in service of one outcome: teams that scale faster and perform better. You understand how to evaluate whether an executive is the right person for the next stage of growth. You know how to structure a go-to-market org for efficiency.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for someone who loves rolling up their sleeves, thrives in ambiguity, and can credibly advise both a CHRO and broader Executive team.



Key Responsibilities

 - Define (and for key roles, run) the executive hiring process across portfolio companies.

 - Partner with portfolio company CHROs to assess organization health and recommend structural, talent, and capability improvements.

 - Design and conduct assessments of executive & GTM leaders, making clear, time-pressured recommendations on whether leaders are right for the next stage of growth.

 - Design and evolve org structures aligned to stage, growth goals, and business model — including spans of control, coverage ratios, and role architecture.

 - Advise on hiring profiles, interview processes, and onboarding approaches for critical GTM roles.

 - Identify repeatable talent and org design best practices that can be leveraged across the Turn/River portfolio.

 - Act as a visible, trusted representative of Turn/River with portfolio leadership teams.



Qualifications

 - 10+ years of experience, with meaningful depth in People, Talent, or Organizational Effectiveness — significant exposure to GTM and sales organizations is a plus.

 - Ability to assess executive leadership with rigor: making clear, defensible recommendations on leadership fit within 30-60 days of engagement.

 - History of working closely alongside a CHRO or CPO, with proven ability to influence without authority across complex org change initiatives.

 - Nice to have: Exposure to commercial environments with fluency in comp plan design, quota-setting, territory structure, and coverage modeling.

 - Nice to have: Prior experience as a Talent Partner, Operating Partner, or VP Talent at a PE or VC firm — or equivalent experience conducting executive assessments in a high-stakes, time-pressured context.

Founded in 2012 and based in San Francisco, Turn/River has $5.6bn in committed capital and invests globally with a focus on North America and Europe.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Director, Channel Sales to join the Operations team. This person will have two primary responsibilities:

 1. Alongside the other Turn/River operating team members, own and continuously contribute to the Turn/River Channel playbook. This playbook serves as the best practices guide for our network of portfolio companies in how to accelerate each element of Channel sales (new logo, expansion and renewals), from pipeline generation to a closed sale, in a B2B/SaaS environment. 

 2. Partner with Channel leaders (Channel Chiefs to line managers) from a subset of Turn/River’s portfolio companies and support them to over-achieve their Channel sales targets. You will aim to do this with structural and process improvements on key growth levers categorized by Turn/River as either Volume (pipeline creation $), Conversion (by stage %) or Price (AOV and/or contract terms).

 - Partner with the Channel leaders at Turn/River portfolio companies to drive revenue growth, provide guidance, and support implementation of best practices

We are seeking an AI Engineer to build the AI and automation layer of our revenue operations—designing, building, and shipping intelligent workflows that make our sales, renewal, and retention motions faster, more predictable, and scalable. Ultimately, this role is helping the Customer and Sales organizations deliver more revenue sustainably.



This is a building role where you will embed with portfolio company revenue teams and bring a point of view on where AI can create the most leverage—spanning pipeline creation + advancement, forecasting, renewal automation, churn prediction, and more—then re-engineer those workflows using AI agents, LLM-powered tools, and automation frameworks. You will build working systems, put them into production, and iterate based on real performance data.



The ideal candidate is a structured thinker, a relentless builder, and a lifelong learner who thrives on bringing order to complexity. You should be equally comfortable writing a prompt chain as you are configuring a workflow inside of a CRM or revenue intelligence platform, and you should be energized by the challenge of turning a manual, repetitive process into something an AI agent handles autonomously.




Key Responsibilities

 - AI Agent Design & Development: Design, build, and ship autonomous AI agents that execute revenue workflows end to end—including lead qualification, opportunity scoring, account health monitoring, renewal triggers, and win/loss analysis—with minimal human intervention. You will be the one writing the code.

 - Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with Turn/River’s sales, customer success, and finance leads, as well as the data team and portfolio companies, as a thought partner on how AI can accelerate revenue growth, retention, and renewal performance.

 - Workflow Identification & Re-Engineering: Bring a systematic lens to revenue operations, identifying high-value automation opportunities across the full customer lifecycle. Decompose manual workflows—from pipeline creation to renewal processing—into agent-ready components: skills, tools, evaluation frameworks, and feedback loops.

 - Portfolio Company Collaboration: On a project basis, partner directly with portfolio company revenue teams on specific initiatives—for example, building and testing AI-powered workflows that support a portfolio company’s sales productivity, renewal automation, or churn reduction programs.

 - Pipeline & Forecast Analytics: Build AI-assisted reporting and forecasting frameworks that provide real-time visibility into pipeline health, deal velocity, and revenue risk. Surface insights that help sales and CS leadership identify gaps, prioritize accounts, and improve forecast accuracy.

 - Renewal & Retention Automation: Design and deploy intelligent workflows that automate the renewal cycle—including proactive risk identification, renewal outreach sequencing, expansion opportunity detection, and churn propensity modeling—to protect and grow net revenue retention.

 - Frontier AI Adoption: Stay current with the rapidly evolving AI landscape—new models, agent frameworks, and revenue intelligence tooling—and rapidly prototype and deploy new capabilities to keep Turn/River’s revenue function at the cutting edge.



Qualifications

 - Hands-on experience building AI agents, LLM-powered workflows, or intelligent automation systems in a production environment.

 - Individual contributor by preference. You are accountable for building and shipping the work yourself rather than directing others who do — this role is measured in systems running in production, not specifications handed off.

 - Real-world application of AI to improve revenue in a commercial business & extensive knowledge of primary AI platforms

 - Deep familiarity with the B2B SaaS revenue tech stack: CRM platforms (Salesforce or equivalent), revenue intelligence tools, CPQ, and customer success platforms.

 - Data-driven mindset with experience building pipeline dashboards, renewal forecasts, and retention analytics.

 - Structured thinker who can break complex revenue processes into systems of components, root causes, and dependencies.

 - Strong communicator who can distill technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and collaborate effectively with sales and CS leaders.

 - Hands-on, execution-oriented, and accountable for results—this is a building role, not an advisory one.

 - Curious, experimental operator who continuously tests new approaches and technologies.

About Primary

Primary is a seed-stage venture capital firm dedicated to delivering exceptional support to the founders of transformational businesses. By pairing meaningful investment resources with the largest portfolio impact team of any seed investor, our portfolio companies have reached an industry-best seed-to-A graduation rate.



About the Role

We’re hiring an investment associate to help build out our compute practice in San Francisco. Our compute practice sits at the center of the firm’s next chapter - we led the seed round in Etched, now valued at $21B, and have a broader compute portfolio with investments across memory, advanced packaging, quantum, and biological compute.

You will be working directly with Brian Schechter https://www.linkedin.com/in/brian-schechter-1822ba16/ and Gaby Lorenzi https://www.linkedin.com/in/gaby-lorenzi/. You’ll source, diligence, and help originate investments across the full compute stack - including software and hardware opportunities in thermals, advanced packaging, cooling, power, data center management and token efficiency. We’re looking for a technical person, who studied computer science, electrical engineering, or a comparable degree, who has spent time inside startups in the past, and is looking to be a part of building a growing investment practice in one of the most consequential markets of our time – compute. Prior investing experience is not required. Deep technical understanding of compute is also not required.

We're hiring for learning velocity, genuine curiosity about compute, and a deep network in San Francisco to support your growth, not a finished resume. This is a career-defining bet for the right person: help plant Primary's flag in San Francisco and grow into one of the firm's next great investors.

Based in San Francisco, Hybrid in-office 3x/week



What You'll Do

 - Source and build relationships with founders, engineers, and operators across the San Francisco compute and AI ecosystem

 - Run diligence on prospective investments - technical differentiation, competitive dynamics, market sizing - alongside the compute pod

 - Represent Primary and our Compute100 efforts across community events, dinners, and podcast tapings to build the firm's brand and network in the Bay Area

 - Help develop and pressure-test investment theses across the compute stack

 - Support the existing compute portfolio, including Etched, as needed

 - Build and maintain a running map of high-signal people and companies worth tracking

 - Help extend Primary's reach into the technical communities - Neo, top engineering orgs, research labs - that produce the next generation of compute founders



About You

 - Must be available to work full-time in SF with periodic travel to NYC

 - 2-4 years of experience with at least 1-2 years of experience in a production engineering role at a leading tech company, AI lab, or high-growth startup

 - Computer Science degree or equivalent experience

 - Deeply plugged into the San Francisco technical and AI scene

 - Genuine, self-directed curiosity about compute

 - Comfortable operating with real ambiguity and building process where none exists yet

 - Down-to-earth, collaborative, and able to build trust quickly

ABOUT GEORGIAN



Georgian is a Toronto-based venture capital firm that partners with high-growth technology companies across cybersecurity, AI software, robotics, defense. We manage about $6B in assets and we have invested in more than 80 companies that we support with capital and technical capability.



Our in-house AI lab works directly with portfolio companies to provide a differentiated experience across the investment lifecycle, and drives the adoption of AI for our internal operations.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE



This role will represent Georgian at the highest levels of LP engagement, supporting the scale of our platform across Growth Funds, Breakout Funds, and SPVs. It is a senior-facing position with significant exposure to Georgian's Founders and leadership team, requiring a high degree of autonomy, judgment, and executive presence.

Unlike traditional Capital Formation roles, success at Georgian requires the ability to flex across both fundraising and investment functions. The Capital Formation team owns Investor Relations, the firm’s Strategic Investments program (Breakout Fund, LP co-invest, SPVs), and asset allocation. The team includes a mix of fundraisers, relationship managers, portfolio analysts, investment bankers, and investment professionals who specialize in later-stage or complex investment execution. This position offers meaningful exposure to deal execution and syndication across the Breakout Fund, LP co-invests, and SPVs (alongside core LP relationship management).

 




WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR





LP COVERAGE & RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT

 - Serve as both primary and secondary relationship manager across the LP base:
   
   - Own a defined set of relationships directly while supporting the Head of Capital Formation and Georgian’s Founders as a secondary point of contact on their pipeline.
   
   - Core coverage focused on North America, however potential travel across the Middle East, Europe, and Asia may be needed.

 - Maintain active LP engagement through regular calls, meetings, conferences, and roadshows. Track sentiment and preferences to tailor communications and strengthen long-term partnerships.

 - Act as a key execution partner to the Head of Capital Formation by preparing briefing materials, talking points, and presentations.

 - Step in to represent the Head of Capital Formation where appropriate, and provide strategic input to support fundraising decisions and LP prioritization.

 - Support development and execution of fundraising strategy, including identification and prioritization of new LP prospects.

 - Prepare pipeline reports and status updates for senior leadership, providing visibility into fundraising progress and conversion metrics.




CAPITAL FORMATION OPERATIONS

 - Oversee the strategy of core LP communications and partner with various firm stakeholders to drive execution.

 - Help build scalable processes, templates, and playbooks that improve team efficiency and output quality.

 - Delegate, mentor, and oversee work products from junior team members, providing feedback to ensure quality, consistency, and professional development.

 - Coordinate due diligence processes for prospective investors, including DDQ responses, reference calls, and onsite visits, with support from junior Capital Formation resources.

 - Partner with finance, legal, and compliance teams to support LP reporting obligations and regulatory requirements.




STRATEGIC INVESTMENT SYNDICATION

During periods when Georgian is not actively raising a flagship fund, we believe LP facing team members should develop deeper expertise across our portfolio and investment strategy. In our view, the best way to build that expertise is through hands-on deal execution, which sharpens the investor mindset needed to engage LPs with conviction and credibility. Our co-invest program is a critical tool for deepening LP relationships, and having genuine depth on our portfolio and strategy is what makes those conversations meaningful.

 - Support the Strategic Investments team across large follow-on investments derived from our Breakout Fund, LP co-invest opportunities, and SPVs or Continuation Vehicles.

 - Collaborate with the Strategic Investments team on deal materials (investment memos, ad hoc due diligence requests, cap table analysis, company presentations), transaction structuring, diligence coordination, and closing mechanics.

 - When required, Interact with portfolio company management teams on transaction process milestones, syndication, and closing dynamics.

 - Serve as a primary point of contact for LP co-invest interest, matching opportunities to investor mandates and managing communication throughout the investment process.

 - Build and maintain relationships with LPs and strategic partners to develop a reliable syndication network for future co-invest opportunities.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR



 - Experience: 5+ years of experience in investment banking, a top-tier placement agent firm, management consulting, or a dedicated investor relations/business development role within private equity.

 - Intellectual Curiosity: you demonstrate a genuine passion for software and AI trends, with an eagerness to master complex technical concepts quickly. You will proactively engage with subject matter experts in the AI Lab to stay ahead of market shifts and firm-wide innovations.

 - Analytical Rigor: you apply a first-principles mindset to evaluate business fundamentals and technical differentiation. You are expected to synthesize deep diligence insights to confidently contribute in discussions both internally and to sophisticated LPs.

 - Technical Skills: You must demonstrate high proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets (financial modeling/metrics) and PowerPoint/Google Slides, supported with strong technical experience managing and interpreting large data sets, data analysis, data mining, and pattern recognition. High proficiency using AI productivity tools to streamline workflows and accelerate content development is a significant asset. Experience withHubSpot, Deal Cloud, or similar CRM workflows for pipeline tracking is a nice-to-have asset.

 - Soft Skills: You possess the professional polish and confidence required to navigate high-stakes environments and “manage the room” during senior level engagements. You command credibility with institutional executives while maintaining obsessive attention to detail, and the ability to execute complex projects under tight deadlines.

 - Education: Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, commerce, or a related field.




LOCATION & WORK ARRANGEMENT



 - Work Environment: This role is hybrid, but the head office is based in Toronto. Georgian’s hybrid work model balances focused remote work with high-impact in-office collaboration.

 - Travel: This position requires a strong willingness to travel globally (estimated to be up to 50-60% time commitment) to support investor meetings and industry conferences.

 - Growth: This is a high-visibility role with significant exposure to senior leadership and the global LP community, offering a clear path towards a Partner level role within Capital Formation.




POSITION STATUS



This posting represents an active, immediate vacancy on our team. We are currently interviewing for this role.




OUR COMMITMENT TO ACCESSIBILITY



Georgian is dedicated to building an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. We provide reasonable accommodations throughout our recruitment process to ensure every candidate has the opportunity to perform at their best. If you require any specific accommodations at any stage, please reach out to us at peopleteam [at]  georgian.io.




USE OF AI



Innovation is at our core and we use artificial intelligence (AI) to support parts of our hiring process, such as screening and evaluating applications. These tools are designed to assist - not replace - human decision making and all final hiring decisions are made by our team.  We regularly review our AI tools to help promote fairness and reduce the risk of unintended bias. If you have any questions about how we use AI in our process or would like more information, please contact us at careers [at] georgian.io.

description_plain:
Playground Global is a venture capital firm backing the most technically ambitious founders working at the edge of engineering and science. With over $1.7 billion under management, Playground invests in early-stage companies defining the future of next-generation compute, automation, energy, and engineered biology.

We are seeking an Operating Partner,  Fundraising & Technology who has a track record of successfully identifying and closing lead investors at later-stage technology companies. Our ideal candidate is someone who will be pivotal in guiding and supporting our deep tech portfolio companies (across next-gen computing, AI and automation, logistics and infrastructure, and energy transition), ensuring teams have achieved the necessary business development milestones and customer traction before fundraising, ensuring an optimal outcome for the portfolio company.

You will create relevant commercial, strategic, and knowledge-sharing opportunities/connectivity on commercial positioning, market expansion, industry trends, and perspectives of leading investors and decision-makers.




WHAT YOU’LL DO


FUNDRAISING

 - Collect market intelligence and perform ongoing research on deal activity in Playground Global’s key sectors.

 - Develop a comprehensive fundraising playbook to help Portfolio Companies understand the capital-raising process.

 - Establish yourself as a trusted advisor to Playground Portfolio Companies, offering strategic guidance throughout their funding journeys.

 - Provide expert counsel on the entire funding lifecycle, from initial stages to subsequent rounds. Help identify lead investors and coordinate with Playground's IR team to connect appropriate LPs as follow-on investors.

 - Foster senior executive relationships, including but not limited to CFOs and independent board members.


BUILDING STRATEGIC RELATIONSHIPS

 - Cultivate relationships with later-stage investors, including Venture, Growth, Cross-over, and Secondary investors

 - Support the facilitation of relevant commercial or strategic introductions amongst portfolio companies, network relationships, and prospects.

 - Advise Portfolio Companies on M&A activities, including potential suitable partners and investment strategies; foster strategic relationships for successful M&A and IPO.


ADVISORY SUPPORT

 - Inform portfolio companies on trends and strategic priorities of key customer verticals.

 - Synthesize complex and often disparate qualitative and quantitative data sources to build a narrative around company performance.


CROSS-TEAM COLLABORATION

 - Offer strategic guidance to the investment team, contributing insights on potential investments and M&A opportunities.

 - Collaborate closely with the marketing team to develop and deliver Playground's unique perspective on your area of expertise.

 - Strategize with Playground Investor Relations to identify suitable Limited Partners (LPs) for potential direct investment.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (6-12 MONTHS IN)

 -  Learn the portfolio and what the companies need to accomplish to achieve a successful fundraise or exit

 -  Network with later-stage capital who can write lead term sheets in follow on rounds

 - Attend relevant banker and industry events to ensure the portfolio is networking among relevant stakeholders

 - Assist portfolio companies in the creation of data rooms and financial models in preparation of fundraising, strategic partnerships, and acquisition conversations




SKILLS & TRAITS

 - You have 10+ years of relevant experience showcasing expertise in leading capital-raising efforts from initial outreach through due diligence, valuation, and structuring for technology companies.

 - Ideal experience can be derived from investment banking, corporate development, or venture capital backgrounds.

 - You have a track record of successfully identifying and closing lead investors at later-stage technology companies.

 - You have a strong network and the ability to build and maintain connectivity with investors, acquirers, and advisors.

 - You possess strong written and verbal communication. Independent executor who has strong collaboration skills. Solid project management skills among both internal and external constituents. Dream up new creative ways to be a champion for the success of Playground companies.

 - You can think creatively and devise innovative deal approaches and solutions to address complex challenges.



The job is based in Palo Alto, California, and is not eligible for remote status. Travel is required for this position, on average 20% of the time a quarter.



The annual base salary range is $300,000 to $425,000. This range represents the low and high end of this California-based position's anticipated base salary range. The base salary will depend on numerous factors such as experience, knowledge, and skills.



This role is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. The company will not sponsor applicants for work visas, nor will it transfer existing visas, for this position now or in the future.



We believe great ideas come from diverse perspectives, and we’re committed to building a team that reflects the world we live in. If you’re passionate about our work, we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and experiences and encourage individuals of all identities to apply.



E-Verify Participation

Playground Global participates in E-Verify. This means we will provide the Social Security Administration (SSA) and, if necessary, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), with information from each new employee's Form I-9 to confirm work authorization. For more information on E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please see the E-Verify Participation Poster https://www.e-verify.gov/sites/default/files/everify/posters/EVerifyParticipationPoster.pdf and Right to Work Poster https://www.e-verify.gov/sites/default/files/everify/posters/IER_RightToWorkPoster%20Eng_Es.pdf.

description_plain:
ABOUT FIRST ROUND

First Round https://firstround.com/ is a venture capital firm that works with founders exclusively at the earliest stages of company building, often when all they have is an “imagine if.” We fill in where we can until the team is filled out, tackling crucial early hiring and equipping those who are great at building product with the skills to sell it, too. By getting the foundational firsts right, we increase the odds of finding extreme product-market fit. Our founders’ “imagine ifs” have turned into companies like Notion, Roblox, Uber, and Square.


ABOUT THE ROLE

One of the most important jobs our team does is to help founders generate and execute their first few dozen sales conversations and pave the path for founders to get to their first million in ARR. That’s what our Founding GTM does.

This role is First Round's embedded, interim "founding GTM" for our portfolio. You'll work across 3–5 portfolio companies at a time, dropping into each one as if you were their first outbound hire — clarify ICP, figure out the right outbound strategy, build a target list, run and iterate on campaigns to book meetings for the founder to take from there. You might cold call 50 prospects on a Monday, build outbound sequences on Tuesday, and hand-deliver gifts to top prospect accounts on a Wednesday.

Why this opportunity is unique: If you're a future founder or Sales Leader, this is one of the best apprenticeships you'll find. You’ll work with the top founders in SF and NYC, learn from our VP of GTM/Founder Success — a GTM veteran with 20+ years of tech sales leadership experience — and have first dips on founding GTM roles at First Round companies after 18 months in the role.




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Serve as the embedded founding GTM for 3–5 portfolio companies simultaneously, each at a different stage of building out their own outbound motion.

 - For each company, define the ICP with the founder, build and continuously refine and enrich target account/contact lists and launch multi-channel outbound (email, LinkedIn, phone) under that company's brand and voice. You’ll have the freedom and budget to try lots of tactics to get meetings.

 - Write and iterate outbound messaging and sequences per company. Each engagement gets its own ICP-specific copy and cadence, no AI slop. Treat messaging as a live experiment: test hooks, subject lines, and CTAs against reply and booked-meeting rate, and kill what's underperforming within days, not weeks.

 - Keep CRM/tracker hygiene tight across every engagement and report weekly meeting volume, pipeline, and conversion against goals for each company.

 - Manage the split across 3–5 concurrent engagements — triage your hours weekly toward whichever company's pipeline needs it most, without letting any one go quiet.

 - Hand off cleanly: when a company hires its own BDR or AE, transfer the playbook, lists, and messaging that worked, then roll onto the next portfolio company.

 - This is a hybrid role based in either our San Francisco or New York office, with 3 days per week on-site.




YOU COULD BE GREAT IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 1–3 years in a high performance environment successfully doing outbound/BDR motions at a startup — ideally as a founding or early BDR who built the pipeline engine, not someone who worked inside one someone else built.

 - Are very comfortable with ambiguity, continuous iteration and imperfection. You don’t need a playbook to follow to get the job done.

 - Know how to combine the right channel, prospect, messaging hook to get the conversion

 - Exceptional urgency and extreme autonomy. You can go from defining ICP → identifying signals → list building → message writing / personalization → campaign launch in a few hours, with no hand holding.

 - Deep fluency in AI-native prospecting — signal/intent-based targeting, enrichment waterfalls, and using LLMs to research an account or persona in minutes, not hours.

 - Fluency in all modern outreach tools and approaches including Claude, Clay, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Instantly/Lemlist/Apollo, Ploy.ai http://Ploy.ai, HubSpot/Salesforce or similar CRM).

 - Very strong written communication skills — comfortable being the outbound voice for several different companies and ICPs in the same week. A sharp editorial eye for AI output: you can spot "AI slop" instantly and edit it out.

 - Extreme organization — able to run 3–5 concurrent outbound engagements without dropping details.

 - Genuine excitement to work on the front lines of early stage startups. Comfortable with ambiguity and fast context-switching between very different products, ICPs, and founders week to week.


OUR VALUES

At First Round, we value resourcefulness, team-play, excellence and hustle. To give you a sense of what our team is all about, check out our values that guide our work:

 - Try harder for founders. They’re our customers — LPs are our shareholders. We go to the ends of the earth for our founders. You might think our role as venture capitalists is to simply maximize returns. But at First Round, we believe when we put founders first, everything will follow — epic returns included. We fill in the gaps on a founder's team before they even have one and get to work on the unglamorous tasks that actually move companies forward. We'll know we've done our job when they're left feeling startled that an investor would go to these lengths for them.

 - Take the wheel. Welcome to First Round. Everything is now your responsibility. Cartographers, not navigators, are the ones who tend to do well here. There are no career ladders to climb or boxes to check at First Round. If you find ways to do more for the business and our customers, your role will naturally expand alongside it. First Round is a haven for people who see themselves as architects of their reality, not casualties of circumstance. We know we have agency over our agency, and we make the conscious choice to exercise it every day.

 - Treat the little things like big things. “Magic is just someone spending more time on something than anyone else might reasonably expect.” We’re all about the carefully crafted, the nitty-gritty, and the bespoke. Whether it’s hand cutting each nameplate, or debating the optimal shape of the dinner table, no detail is too small to sweat. This is decidedly not a "LGTM" culture. It is a culture where the little things are the big things.

 - Give your unvarnished opinions and unwavering support. We strive to be kind, not nice. Being nice and being kind are not one and the same. In our view, kindness means being generous, helpful, and compassionate. Nice can be used as a convenient shortcut; kindness cultivates long-term excellence. One of the most (counterintuitively) compassionate things you can do is to offer your unvarnished opinion — along with your unwavering support. That willingness to risk a fleeting moment of discomfort in exchange for someone else’s growth is long-term kindness. So while we strive to be a founder’s coach in the corner, part of that responsibility requires being the kick in the ass when they need it most. We try to be as honest as possible in every encounter, whether that’s bluntly telling a founder how they can step up their game, or delivering radical candor in our feedback for teammates.

 - Invent and wander. “Action produces information." We’re fans of starting small, shipping fast, and obsessively improving. The idea for the First Round Review wasn’t the product of a six-month strategy session — we wrote up a few blog posts and just shipped them. That’s because reality has a surprising amount of detail and edges that are difficult to anticipate. Each step — even the wrong one — reveals new information that improves your next move. We prefer to make the gap between having an idea and knowing if it works as small as possible.

description_plain:
ABOUT SOUND VENTURES

At Sound, we believe inspiration beats convention, and that the best founders aren’t just solving problems; they’re rewriting the rules.

For the last 15 years, we’ve invested thematically in category-defining companies at the forefront of major technology platform shifts. We seek out founders with relentless ambition and bold ideas, backing them before the rest of the world sees what’s coming.

Our portfolio includes early investments in Affirm, Airbnb, Airtable, Anthropic, Duolingo, EquipmentShare, GitLab, OpenAI, SentinelOne, and Uber, among others.

Sound Ventures is led by General Partners Effie Epstein and Guy Oseary and manages $2B+ across a series of funds.




THE ROLE

We're looking for a force-multiplier — someone who sits at the intersection of Chief of Staff and Business Operations and makes the entire team more effective. This role doesn't fit neatly into a job description because the work won't either. You'll own high-priority initiatives, drive operational rigor, and serve as a trusted thought partner to firm leadership and founders.

The defining requirement: you must be genuinely AI-native. Not AI-curious — AI-proficient. You deploy AI tools daily to do the work of multiple people, identify where AI can unlock leverage across the firm, and help us build a culture where that's the norm, not the exception.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

•       Serve as a strategic partner across the firm  — managing priorities, preparing for key meetings, and ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.

•       Lead cross-functional projects that cut across investing, portfolio support, marketing, incubations, and finance

•      Build internal AI-powered processes to own the operating cadence: team rhythms, firm-wide communications, and follow-through on key decisions.

•       Identify and implement AI tools and workflows that meaningfully increase the team's leverage and output quality.

•       Identify operational bottlenecks and design solutions before they become problems.

•       Stay at the frontier of what's possible and bring those capabilities to the firm before we know we need them.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

•       5–7 years of experience in venture capital, investment banking, management consulting, or a high-growth startup in a strategy or operations role

•       Demonstrably AI-native: you use AI tools as a core part of your daily workflow and can show your work.

•       Exceptional written and verbal communicator — you can distill complex ideas crisply and confidently

•       A builder's mindset: you don't wait for systems to exist, you create them.

•       High emotional intelligence and the judgment to navigate conversations across the organization, as well as with  founders, LPs, and partners.

•       Comfort operating in ambiguity — this role will evolve and you'll help define it.

•       Low ego, high ownership. You're equally comfortable setting the strategy and executing the details as part of a small team




NICE TO HAVE

•       Prior experience in venture capital or working directly with a GP or founder.

•       A Marketer’s mindset  We are a Marketing-leaning firm that thinks and works creatively.




LOCATION & COMPENSATION

This job is based in Los Angeles, CA. Potential for LA/SF hybrid. Competitive salary, carry eligibility, and benefits commensurate with experience.

description_plain:
Voleon is a technology company that applies state-of-the-art AI and machine learning techniques to real-world problems in finance. For nearly two decades, we have led our industry and worked at the frontier of applying AI/ML to investment management. We have become a multibillion-dollar asset manager, and we have ambitious goals for the future.



Your colleagues will include internationally recognized experts in artificial intelligence and machine learning research as well as highly experienced finance and technology professionals. In addition to our enriching and collegial working environment, we offer highly competitive compensation and benefits packages, technology talks by our experts, a beautiful modern office, daily catered lunches, and more.

 

As a Member of Research Staff, you will work at the forefront of modern statistical machine learning. Your research colleagues have collectively published hundreds of academic articles in top-tier venues on machine learning, systems, and theory, and we meet regularly to stay current on the latest academic research and share ideas. Founded in 2007 by two leading scientists (see management bios https://voleon.com/management/), http://voleon.com/about/management-2/ Voleon supports a culture of curiosity, collegiality, and creativity.

 

Your work will focus on financial market prediction and portfolio optimization. The behavior of financial markets is noisy and violates a number of classical statistical assumptions, and we’ve spent over a decade pioneering scientific advances in the application of machine learning techniques to this domain. You will work with a complex and diverse array of datasets to implement and iterate on predictive models. Predicting financial markets is an enduringly hard problem, but results are immediate and unambiguous.

 

Years of academic training has prepared you for this moment. You won’t just conduct research, you’ll apply it on a daily basis, working with a team across the entire life cycle of applied research problems. Your work will span from basic research to productizing solutions and validating their efficacy in live trading. This role is a means to make a difference: you will help direct billions of dollars in trades daily while making an enduring impact on our field.

 

*** Relocation and work visa eligibility for qualified candidates***




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Develop a rich understanding of Voleon’s challenges and methodologies and propose research innovations and experiments to build, maintain and optimize the models that govern our investment strategy

 - Prepare and analyze new datasets to assess their predictive efficacy

 - Develop, validate, and implement new models into production

 - Design and conduct experiments to improve simulations and evaluate the success of new models in a live environment

 - Communicate and collaborate effectively with other Members of Research Staff and Software Engineers at each stage, driving progress towards tangible outcomes

 - Keep up to date on the latest academic research to identify novel approaches to explore for application to our domain




REQUIREMENTS

 - Background in modern statistical methods and machine learning with a track record as an applied researcher

 - Evidence of strong mathematical abilities (e.g., publication record, graduate coursework, or competition placement)

 - Interest in software development techniques and willingness to write production level code (Python and/or R preferred)

 - Ability to solve large-scale computing problems

 - Eagerness to work in collaborative and diverse teams

 - Interest in financial applications is essential, but prior finance industry experience is not a pre-requisite

 - Ph.D. level coursework is required, and a Ph.D. degree in a relevant field is preferred

description_plain:
About BlockTech

BlockTech is an algorithmic trading firm operating at the frontier of global crypto derivatives and spot markets. We trade 24/7 across some of the fastest-moving, most data-rich venues in finance.

Crypto is one of the few markets where the gap between a good model and live PnL comes down to how fast and how reliably you can ship it. Abundant data, novel microstructure, and a short path to production mean the quality of our infrastructure directly moves the edge. We're looking for a Quantitative Developer to build that infrastructure and get our models into production.



The role

This is a hands-on  engineering seat on our trading floor. You'll own the infrastructure that turns research models into production trading systems, working primarily in Python and Rust, the language our models and systems are written in. You'll build the frameworks and tooling that let quants ship their code to production and keep those systems running once they're live.

You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with researchers, traders, and fellow engineers, building the tooling, pipelines, and standards that let good ideas reach production quickly and safely, and helping raise the engineering bar across the floor.



You will

 - Build and own the infrastructure that takes models from research to production - data pipelines, backtesting, deployment, and monitoring.

 - Turn research prototypes into robust, performant, production-grade code that runs reliably in live trading

 - Work closely with quantitative researchers and traders to get new models live quickly and safely

 - Own the systems you ship in production: monitor performance, diagnose issues, and keep latency and reliability high

 - Improve the tools, standards, and pipelines the team relies on, raising the engineering bar across the floor
   

What we're looking for

 - 2+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of shipping production-grade systems

 - A strong academic foundation in a STEM discipline (computer science, mathematics, physics, engineering, or similar)

 - Strong programming skills in Python and ideally Rust and/or C++.

 - Solid software engineering fundamentals: clean, testable, maintainable code, version control, testing, and CI/CD

 - The ability to collaborate with researchers and traders and translate research code into production systems

 - Clear written and verbal English
   

Strong Pluses

 - Experience building or maintaining trading, backtesting, or data infrastructure

 - Familiarity with market microstructure, or an interest in learning how trading systems work end-to-end
   

What's in it for you?

 - Real ownership and a direct line to live PnL. Research, engineering, and trading happen a few metres apart, with the shortest feedback loops in the industry.

 - Competitive base salary plus a very attractive performance-based bonus tied to individual and company results

 - For strong performers, the opportunity to buy into the trading fund

 - A floor of strong peers and minimal bureaucracy between a good idea and production

 - Annual learning & development budget and an in-house training program

 - Pension plan, company laptop, and reimbursement of home internet costs

 - Gym membership reimbursement and sports during working hours (kickboxing, CrossFit, fitness, soccer)

 - Daily breakfast and warm lunch, with snacks and drinks throughout the day

 - Regular socials: weekly Friday drinks, monthly outings, quarterly sports competitions, bi-annual trips abroad

 - For internationals: an all-in relocation package and Dutch classes




OUR CULTURE

At our core, we are a team of passionate trading and tech enthusiasts committed to revolutionizing trading through automation. Our collaborative approach ensures that everyone contributes to achieving our ambitious goals.

In this role, you will be both challenged and stretched, with ample opportunities for growth and development, both within and beyond your main responsibilities.

We invest in our people by offering competitive compensation and benefits, fostering innovation, and celebrating success. Our commitment to personal development transcends traditional norms; we provide an equal playing field, promote reverse leadership, and offer boundless growth opportunities for all our employees.

Join us to unlock your potential and drive innovation in the exciting world of algorithmic trading.

description_plain:
ABOUT BLOCKTECH

As a Quantitative Trader on our Singapore trading floor, you’ll own positions and PnL end-to-end, from interpreting live market flow and liquidity through tuning and intervening in our automated systems, all the way to shaping the next generation of execution logic and trading tools.

You’ll sit shoulder-to-shoulder with Quantitative Researchers, Quantitative Developers, and Software Engineers, and your decisions will directly drive how we trade across venues.




THE ROLE

 - Managing and monitoring D1 positions across multiple venues, owning the PnL and risk that comes with them

 - Reading live market flow, liquidity conditions, and market events, and translating that read into concrete trading and execution decisions

 - Tuning and parameterising our automated and semi-automated systems, and knowing when to step in to manage risk or capture an opportunity

 - Improving execution quality and market-making performance through data-driven analysis of strategy behaviour

 - Designing and specifying the trading tools, dashboards, and analytics that the desk relies on to make decisions

 - Collaborating closely with researchers, developers, and engineers to sharpen models, infrastructure, and execution logic, and shaping the roadmap for new trading initiatives




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years of experience as a Quantitative Trader and/or Quantitative Researcher in a professional trading environment, with demonstrated PnL responsibility on linear (D1) products across multiple venues

 - Hands-on experience operating automated and semi-automated trading systems under live conditions: monitoring, tuning, and intervening when it matters

 - Strong analytical instincts: you can take a messy dataset of fills and quotes and turn it into a concrete execution improvement

 - A deep, intuitive grasp of market microstructure and the ability to explain why a strategy works, not just that it does

 - Proficiency in Python for analysis, tooling, and interaction with trading systems

 - An ownership mindset: being proactive, accountable, and comfortable making decisions with immediate financial impact

 - Clear written and verbal English, and the ability to communicate effectively with traders, researchers, and engineers

Nice to have

 - Exposure to systematic HFT and MFT strategies, ideally in Crypto D1 markets




WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?

 - A seat on a trading floor in the heart of Singapore’s CBD, where trading, research, and engineering are closely aligned with short feedback loops and direct impact on live PnL

 - Competitive compensation consisting of a base salary combined with a very attractive bonus plan based on individual and company performance

 - Outstanding performance is rewarded with the opportunity to buy into the trading fund

 - Company laptop, home office budget, and transportation allowance

 - An extensive in-house training program and an annual learning & development budget

 - The opportunity to work at the forefront of automated trading using state-of-the-art technology, in an environment that embraces AI to both accelerate productivity and advance our systems and models

 - Gym membership reimbursement, sports event reimbursement, and the opportunity to do sports during working hours

 - Regular social events, including frequent outings and bi-annual trips abroad

 - Daily breakfast and warm lunch. Additionally, snacks and drinks are provided throughout the day

 - For internationals: All-in relocation package




OUR CULTURE

At our core, we are a team of passionate trading and tech enthusiasts committed to revolutionizing trading through automation. Our collaborative approach ensures that everyone contributes to achieving our ambitious goals.

In this role, you will be both challenged and stretched, with ample opportunities for growth and development, both within and beyond your main responsibilities.

We invest in our people by offering competitive compensation and benefits, fostering innovation, and celebrating success. Our commitment to personal development transcends traditional norms; we provide an equal playing field, promote reverse leadership, and offer boundless growth opportunities for all our employees.

Join us to unlock your potential and drive innovation in the exciting world of algorithmic trading.

- Experience identifying and resolving discrepancies, including advocating for a position with an external party using supporting data.
- Proficiency in, or ability to ramp quickly on, Xero and ADP for both US and Canada payroll.
Work location and geographic eligibility:

description_plain:
We are a data-driven company with a collegial atmosphere looking for team members who can do great work for application in the algorithmic trading industry.



NumerixS Quant builds quantitative trading strategies grounded in science and driven by technology. With a team of scientists, mathematicians, and physicists, we design and run systematic trading strategies grounded in rigorous academic research.

We are seeking a Controller who will be solely responsible for the accounting function and PNL reconciliation, serving as a financial business partner to leadership. Our ideal candidate is a hands-on, independent accounting professional with hedge fund experience who quickly builds strong working relationships with stakeholders.

This opportunity will be remote, based in Texas.



About you

You've built a career in hedge fund or alternative investment accounting, have owned the full accounting cycle, and you're ready to take that ownership to the next level as a solo operator. You're motivated by running the whole function and taking full accountability for its accuracy, integrity, and controls, not just executing within it. You’re self-directed and think like an owner: anticipating issues before they surface, setting the processes others will follow, and being the final word on the numbers.



What You’ll Do

Full ownership of the accounting function, including books, records, and internal controls, maintained in Xero.

 - Own the monthly PNL reconciliation process with investors, confidently identifying and resolving discrepancies to ensure the firm’s numbers are accurate and well-supported. If the numbers don’t line up, you’re the one who digs in, makes the case, and doesn’t back down until it’s resolved correctly.

 - Build strong, trust-based relationships with clients and stakeholders, to quickly and efficiently resolve discrepancies.

 - Review and approve all supplier invoices, with an eye toward cost control and ensuring the firm is never overpaying for expenses, resolving discrepancies if they arise.

 - Manage payroll across the US and Canada using ADP, accurately and on schedule.

 - Ensuring the accounting books, records and related internal controls are appropriate for audit.

 - Design, document, and maintain accounting policies and internal controls appropriate for the company’s size and regulatory environment.

 - Own everything that touches money, including managing bank accounts, all ad hoc banking tasks, transfers, and money-related HR tasks.



What You Bring

 - 7+ years of accounting experience, including prior experience owning a full accounting function inside a hedge fund or alternative investment fund.

 - Hands-on general ledger ownership, running books independently without oversight.

 - Experience reconciling internal PNL to an external party’s calculation.

 - Demonstrated ability to identify and resolve discrepancies with confidence, including experience advocating for a position with an external party and supporting it with clear, accurate data.

 - Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to maintain productive working relationships even in the context of firm, direct communication.

 - Proficiency or fast ability to ramp on Xero and ADP for both US and Canada payroll.

 - Comfortable being the sole finance person in the building — no backup, no team to lean on.



What We Offer

 - Annual bonus eligibility based on performance

 - Extended healthcare coverage

 - 401(k) matching up to 9% (maximum annual contribution of $13,250)*
